KERB:

Mission runner · game design map

The second trip through the Griptap & Co cabinet. Inside, every program rides a route: its name and its right to ride. Yours is provisional, licensed by the dispatcher VESS. The packets you carry are riders' routes, sold to SABLE, and the last line in the ledger is your own. Three chapters, eighteen jobs, four duels on the Grid.

Platform
iPhone, landscape, iOS 18+, Backbone or any pad, touch fallback; the same code on macOS 15+. SwiftUI + RealityKit + Metal, no packages
Genre
Scrolling hover-racer jobs (delivery, sweep, escape, salvage, dive) plus a Tron light-cycle arena for the duels. Tron-clean, single player
Session
50–88 s corridor windows · duels first to 2 or 3 · free play without a clock
Dev loop
Claude Code builds, verifies with captures, the simulator and 19 headless tests, pushes a Release build to the iPhone 12; you judge by thumb
Source
GDD_2026-10-17.md read against master (PR #6); PR #7 claude/garage noted where it changes a number

One bar

Hull and boost fuel are the same resource, so speed costs safety and what is left at the drop pays.

Every run is a job

A window, a streak score, a payout; the story arrives in briefs, debriefs and the message log, never in cutscenes.

Same-frame acks

Every action is visible, audible and haptic on the frame it happens: pips, stamps, a cue, a rumble.

Procedural worlds, authored cast

Three generated districts, one authored vehicle, KERB's four riders and four named rivals.

KERB's systems, ported 18 Oct (step 2). Thirteen rule cards, once each, the world waiting under them: the job card, one per kind (the Grid's before the rival intro), the first respawn, the first lost round, then one per briefing for the goal card, the garage, the first side offer, the notebook. Story and chapters

Three chapters, eighteen jobs. A chapter opens when the one before it is fully cleared; inside a chapter the first job opens the next two, each job after that needs one more cleared, and a duel waits for every job before it. Tap jobs to clear them and watch the rule.

Outer frame · the Griptap & Co opening

  1. Night. The same corner shop, the same cabinet by the window. The rain has not let up since last time.
  2. “You kids back again? Ha! It's been a while.”
  3. “Well, if you're looking for the board to own, this one's it… the Kerbie Astro. No wheels. Doesn't need 'em where it's going.”
  4. “Oh, I see you eyeing that game again. Didn't you learn your lesson the first time?”
  5. “DIDN'T WASTE ANY TIME, HUH?!?!” (flash, shake) …and the cabinet takes another one. Only this time the machine is bigger.
  6. You were at the cabinet. Now you're in it. Again. The routes are the currency here. Run them.

Voices

Every line of text comes from a named voice in a known register. Comms rule: at most three lines per job, eight words or fewer, never at the objective.

Rules that bite

  • An idle pad does not own the steering: touch and keyboard still work with a pad connected (dead zone 0.12).
  • Boost disarms at 2 % energy and re-arms at 15 %, so a held trigger on an empty hull does not flicker.
  • Cruise speed is locked at 45 m/s while a job is live; the windows and the pursuer are tuned to it.
  • A hit takes 40 % of the speed, 70 ms of hit-stop, a 0.45 s sideways recoil and a bite of the bar.
  • The lane limit is ± 6.9 m; pressing it (or a conduit wall) scrapes at 0.08 bar / s.
  • The Backbone has no actuators, so the phone's taptics do the haptics; the engine hum follows speed and boost.
  • Demo mode pulses the accept button because a held accept has no edge.

Streak score

A gate every 200 m pays 50 × streak and refunds 1.5 s; a beacon 150 × streak; a kill 25 × streak without climbing; the streak climbs to 8 and a hit resets it. Silver at 40 % and gold at 70 % of the clean run's ceiling. Duels: gold on a win.

Payout = base + 3 × seconds left + 2 × hull % + kind bonus (sweep 40 / beacon, escape 2 / m of gap, salvage 30 / kill, dive the hull bonus again) + score / 20; a replay pays half; a side offer's bonus once. Duels: base + 100 × (wins − losses).

The Grid

A kinematic light cycle on Armagetron's curve: speed is a line you draw. Script a run below and the plot integrates LightCycle.step for the player and the rival.

Match pay (free play)

BUILTCAPTURED

40 × wins + 150 if won + 10 × best grind s, into the same purse as the jobs. First to 3; a duel job sets the target out of reach and reads wins / losses itself.

Rivals and the AI

Skill is reaction, never speed: tick 0.30 / 0.16 / 0.10 s (0.14 / 0.08 / 0.05 when a wall is within 14 + 0.25 × speed m), probe range 55 / 80 / 100 m, noise 8 / 5 / 2, blink 12 / 4 / 0 %. Every tick it probes headings through the hash, adds an occupancy-grid space term (6 m cells), a loop guard, the temper's goal, the zone and the ramps; it respawns 4 s after a derez at the most open spot. Its 0.16 s decisions cannot handle more than 54 m/s: keep the cap.

Credits

One purse. A first clear of all eighteen jobs by a clean rider (the headless balance table, which runs the code's own payout) set against the garage. Replays pay half and free-play matches pay too, so nothing is one-time; this is the ceiling of the first pass.

Worlds

Three districts as three themes. Corridor tracks are composed per job from a recipe of phrases over the full distance; The Grid is a height field of decks and ramps.

Architecture

Swift 5 mode, SwiftUI over a non-AR ARView, RealityKit for rendering, a Metal post pass, LowLevelMesh trails and CustomMaterial shaders. No packages, no server; every constant is Swift and every line of story text is in narrative.json.

GDD §10, §11

Layers

One frame

The scene loop at the display rate (a fixed 60 Hz step in captures); hit-stop scales dt by 0.15 for 70 ms; rebuilds go through requestRebuild(), curtain first, re-queued if one is running.

Performance

BUILTUNJUDGED

iPhone 12 ready 3.9 s after launch in Release (Debug ~4 × slower: the procedural textures are Swift pixel loops). Mac Debug 50–60 fps with the post pass; simulator 60 fps with ~180 arena entities. Phone fps and thermals over a long run are not measured. Four Mac captures at once drop to 15–25 fps.

Persistence · UserDefaults

Progress keys are cleared at every launch (fresh start) unless saved; identity keys stay on RESET PROGRESS. iCloud KV sync: GAP

Testing

  • Tests/MissionLoopTests.swift: 19 tests, a 60 Hz headless loop over MissionRunner with six rider profiles and the balance table
  • xcodebuild test -scheme SpeederProto-macOS with SPEEDER_TESTS=1 (the app becomes a bare host, ~3 s)
  • Captures/polish/capture.sh <dir> <s> ENV=VAL: fixed 60 Hz frames, survives the crash-restore modal and display sleep
  • simshot.sh for simulator HUD sheets; the MCP simulator for touch flows
  • ~45 SPEEDER_* switches: DEMO, MISSION, SCREEN, FLAGS, RESET_PROGRESS, ARENA_*, CAMERA, CHECK_NAN, …
  • No screencapture: frames are written by the post pass and read as PNGs
